**Artemis II** (April 1–11, 2026) flew a crew of four on a [flyby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flyby_(spaceflight) "Flyby (spaceflight)") of the [Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon "Moon"). It was the first crewed flight of the [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA")-led [Artemis program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artemis_program "Artemis program"), the only beyond [low Earth orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Low_Earth_orbit "Low Earth orbit") (LEO) since [Apollo 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_17 "Apollo 17") in 1972, and the only beyond LEO not part of the [Apollo program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_program "Apollo program"). It was also the first crewed flight of the [Space Launch System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Launch_System "Space Launch System") and of the [Orion spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_(spacecraft) "Orion (spacecraft)"), which the crew named ***Integrity***.

Artemis II was crewed by four astronauts: commander [Reid Wiseman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reid_Wiseman "Reid Wiseman"), pilot [Victor Glover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Glover "Victor Glover"), and mission specialist [Christina Koch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Koch "Christina Koch"), all from the [NASA Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA_Astronaut_Corps "NASA Astronaut Corps"), along with mission specialist [Jeremy Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeremy_Hansen "Jeremy Hansen") from the [Canadian Astronaut Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Astronaut_Corps "Canadian Astronaut Corps").[[69]](#cite_note-Artemis_Crew-69) On November 22, 2023, [Jenni Gibbons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenni_Gibbons "Jenni Gibbons") was named as Hansen's backup,[[70]](#cite_note-70) and on July 3, 2024, [Andre Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Douglas "Andre Douglas") was named as the backup for the three NASA astronauts.[[71]](#cite_note-Space.com1-71) Glover became the first [person of color](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Person_of_color "Person of color"), Koch the [first woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women_in_space "Women in space"), Wiseman the oldest person, and Hansen the first non-American to travel around the Moon.

Artemis II lifts off from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on April 1, 2026

The crew arrived at Kennedy Space Center on March 27,[[85]](#cite_note-NASA-2026a-85) and the launch countdown began on March 30.[[86]](#cite_note-86) The mission launched aboard an SLS rocket on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B at 22:35:12 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time") (6:35:12 p.m. [EDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Daylight_Time "Eastern Daylight Time"), local time at the launch site).[[6]](#cite_note-NASA_Launch_Time-6)[[87]](#cite_note-87) It was the first crewed launch from LC-39B since [STS-116](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-116 "STS-116") in 2006.

**SpaceX Crew-11** was the eleventh operational NASA [Commercial Crew Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_Crew_Program "Commercial Crew Program") flight and the 19th crewed orbital flight of a [Crew Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crew_Dragon "Crew Dragon") spacecraft. The mission transported four crew members, [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") astronauts [Zena Cardman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zena_Cardman "Zena Cardman") and [Michael Fincke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Fincke "Michael Fincke"), [JAXA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAXA "JAXA") astronaut [Kimiya Yui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimiya_Yui "Kimiya Yui"), and [Roscosmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roscosmos "Roscosmos") cosmonaut [Oleg Platonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleg_Platonov_(cosmonaut) "Oleg Platonov (cosmonaut)"), to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS). The mission launched on August 1, 2025 and docked with the ISS the next day. On January 8, 2026, NASA announced that the mission would end about a month earlier than planned due to a medical situation involving Fincke.

The eleventh SpaceX operational mission in the [Commercial Crew Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_Crew_Program "Commercial Crew Program") was scheduled for launch on July 31, 2025, but was scrubbed due to weather.[[9]](#cite_note-Robinson-Smith_2025-07-31-9) After a quick turn around, SpaceX was able to launch the mission the next day on August 1, 2025.[[11]](#cite_note-LZ1_Retired-11) At 14 hours, 43 minutes, and 10 seconds, it was the fastest Crew Dragon rendezvous to date[[12]](#cite_note-Space.com-12) before later being surpassed by [SpaceX Crew-13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Crew-13 "SpaceX Crew-13") at 7 hours, 55 minutes, and 10 seconds.

excerpts.text: An international crew of four launched into orbit just before noon Friday from Florida on [NASA's Crew-11](https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-11/), a six-month mission to the [International Space Station](https://www.nasa.gov/international-space-station/).

SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket roared to life on Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39-A, lofting the company's [Dragon capsule](https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/dragon) and crew on a nine-minute trip from the Earth's surface into orbit.

A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket with the Crew Dragon capsule Endeavour carrying the Crew-11 mission lifts off from Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Friday. **Chandan Khanna/AFP via Getty Images** ****hide caption****
It is the first trip to space for mission commander Cardman.
For Crew-11 pilot Mike Fincke, it will be his fourth trip to the space station.
The mission marks the second trip to the station for Japan's Yui Kimiya.

excerpts.text:
NASA’s SpaceX Crew-11 mission safely splashed down early Thursday morning in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, concluding a more than five-month mission aboard the International Space Station.

NASA astronauts [Zena Cardman](https://www.nasa.gov/people/zena-cardman/) and [Mike Fincke](https://www.nasa.gov/people/edward-michael-mike-fincke/), JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) astronaut Kimiya Yui, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Oleg Platonov returned to Earth at 12:41 a.m.

The Crew-11 mission [lifted off](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasas-spacex-crew-11-launches-to-international-space-station/) at 11:43 a.m. EDT on Aug.1, 2025, from Launch Complex 39A at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
